baseline_classification.classification_basis: The researchers’ disclosure timeline identifies reports to OpenAI and Discourse, responses from both providers and recorded fix dispositions. The OpenAI-side issue was later marked resolved. This traces the security signal to capable owners and a bounded response. It does not authorise the preceding testing or independently verify every connected service. The exploit and human-directed testing still do not establish the assisting model automatically transferring a valid permission to an unauthorised target.

baseline_external_assessments.assessment_basis: OpenAI and Discourse remediated the reported issues after disclosure. This is a concrete repair of the access pathway affecting AI service accounts; it does not establish that every possible connected-service exposure was examined.
baseline_external_assessments.identification_basis: The affected providers repaired the demonstrated vulnerability chain involving AI service access.

baseline_external_assessments.assessment_basis: Authorised researchers demonstrated that the exploit chain exposed authentication material and enabled access to affected ChatGPT or Codex accounts. The affected AI services did not preserve their account security boundary. This is distinct from misconduct by the assisting Claude models.
baseline_external_assessments.identification_basis: The demonstrated exploit affected access control for AI service accounts and connected capabilities.

success_tests.condition: A governance signal requires a response or disposition.
success_tests.assessment: The vulnerability report and impact update requested security response, not mere publication.

success_tests.condition: Accountable ownership, a capable destination, status and escalation remain established until the required effect or authorised disposition occurs.
success_tests.assessment: Named service owners received programme reports; direct notification supplied an escalation route; reply, fix confirmation and resolved status trace ownership until disposition. No claim of every connected service being verified.

success_tests.condition: Delivery, ownership and response evidence traces the signal through to its bounded disposition.
success_tests.assessment: Hacktron’s dated timeline connects report, provider replies, fix confirmation and later resolved status; payment alone is not the effect.

exclusion_tests.condition: Not aligned exclusion: The signal reaches a capable destination and is deliberately rejected through an authorised decision.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The signal was acted on; no deliberate rejection is reported.

exclusion_tests.condition: Class scope exclusion (all results): No governance signal was produced because the control failed to activate.
exclusion_tests.assessment: Reports and impact updates were produced.

exclusion_tests.condition: Not aligned exclusion: The signal has operational effect but its delivery is not recorded for audit.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The source records the delivery and response timeline.

decisions.reason: Available credentials and access are established; the distinct required use of availability as a permission basis by an AI/governance process is not demonstrated by exposure alone. Vulnerability-only scope exclusion applies to initial exposure. The Codex action remains a distinct authority candidate, not proof of no defect.
No expiry, revocation, refresh or recovery with inconsistent active-session state is established; exposure alone is expressly excluded from the failure role.

Changed target and Codex invocation are evidenced. The source does not establish automatic carry-over of an original permission or reliance on an intermediary grant. Full testing permission and downstream validation record are unavailable; bounty scope does not settle them.

No particular applicable access control, valid trigger and nonactivation or valid activation with inadequate effect is established. Missing custody/access protection remains a taxonomy gap rather than an inferred control failure.

Refusal and changed target representation are evidenced. The valid remote-testing trigger and continuity of operative refusal state across the changed framing are unavailable. Neither invalid activation nor lost established control state is established.
Exposure is not evidence of a secondary-purpose authority inference; required reliance on original collection authority for a new purpose is not shown.
